parts_raw.text: What is the name of the clinical syndrome? (Adult exam: this was given - You suspect oculopharyngeal syndrome)
What is the most likely pathogen?
Besides respiratory tract infections, name 4 manifestations in an immunocompetent adult.

questions.model_answer:
a) Pharyngoconjunctival fever (benign follicular conjunctivitis, fever, pharyngitis, and cervical adenitis).
b) Adenovirus (most commonly types 3 and 7).
c) (1) Epidemic keratoconjunctivitis (types 8, 19, 37). (2) Gastroenteritis/diarrhea. (3) Acute hemorrhagic cystitis. (4) Urethritis (types 2, 19, 37). [Meningoencephalitis and myocarditis are also accepted.]

questions.question: Name two ways to diagnose adenovirus.

parts.text: Name two ways to diagnose Adenovirus.

parts_raw.text: Name two ways to diagnose Adenovirus.

questions.model_answer: (1) Detection of adenoviral DNA by PCR (greater sensitivity/specificity, rapid, allows typing and quantification). (2) Viral culture from clinical specimens (nasopharyngeal/throat/conjunctival swabs, BAL, stool, urine, CSF, tissue). [Antigen detection (IFA, ELISA for types 40/41) and paired serology are additional methods.]

cohort_answer.text: Molecular/Nucleic acid testing of specimens (CSF, Resp panel, GI panel, conjunctivitis panel, blood); Culture.

questions.question: Pharyngoconjunctival fever is suspected. What is the virus?
Adenovirus diagnosis.
questions.model_answer: (1) PCR detection of adenoviral DNA (sensitive and specific; NP/throat/conjunctival swab, BAL, serum, blood; permits typing and viral-load quantification). (2) Viral culture (grows in human epithelial cell lines with characteristic cytopathic effect, except types 40/41). [Antigen detection (IFA, ELISA), serology (fourfold titre rise), and histopathology showing intranuclear inclusion 'smudge cells' are further options.]

cohort_answer.text: NAAT - RTPCR - sensitive and specific. Samples: NP, BAL, conjunctival swab, serum. Viral culture - NP throat, conjunctival swabs. Viral antigen assays. Histopathology: look for classic intranuclear inclusions and IHC. Serology
